name: The Antler Hall
story: Every hart taken in the Briarwold for a hundred years has left its antlers on this wall, and Alder can tell you the year of each one. The gap in the middle of the wall is deliberate, and it is the size of the Hart of Thorns.
who_was_here: The Wyke line, and two hundred harts.
unique_object: a gap in a wall of antlers, kept clear, exactly the size of one head

name: The Bell Chapter-House
story: The Order sleeps inside a fallen bell. Cadwen took the name Ash when she took the vigil, and her old name is written once, on the inside of the bell, where only someone lying down can read it.
who_was_here: Every Toll-Knight since the Ash Winter, each of whom wrote their old name in the same place.
unique_object: a hundred and seventy old names written on the inside curve of a bell, readable only lying down

name: Mullard's Yellow Door
story: A yellow door, as the trade requires, and behind it a brewer who considers the Tallymen's excise a personal insult and keeps two sets of books about it, one of which is accurate.
who_was_here: His mother, who started the second set of books.
unique_object: two ledgers in the same hand, one of them true, kept in different rooms

name: The Memory-Keeper's Room
story: Cut into the cliff, one window, and a wall of knotted cords: the Rope-Song, every verse of it. There is metre in the song for eight clans and only seven cords, and Dunna will show you the gap if you ask twice.
who_was_here: Every memory-keeper of Clan Kharrow, each of whom added a cord and none of whom added the eighth.
unique_object: a wall of knotted cords with a gap where the eighth verse should hang

name: The Steward's House
story: Merrowby's deeds, weights and grudges live in one room with a brass key that Ellard polishes at noon whether it needs it or not. He is not corrupt. He is worse: he is exact.
who_was_here: Four stewards before him, each of whom left the deed chest fuller.
unique_object: the deed chest, whose lid has a map of Merrowby's fields cut into it, updated with a knife

name: Ashdown's Forge
story: Hallam shoes horses and mends ploughs and has made exactly one sword, which he did not sell and will not talk about. It hangs over the hearth in the house, not the shop, which tells you what he thinks it is.
who_was_here: His father, who made no swords at all, and was happier.
unique_object: one sword hanging over a domestic hearth, unsold, with a name on the blade that is not a Vale name

name: The Bell-Keeper's House
story: Seventeen small bells, one for each founding family, and Hesta keeps them all: oiled, rehung, rung on the right days. Two of the seventeen are buried under the Long Table's foot. She still oils the hooks they hung from.
who_was_here: Her aunt, who taught her which bell is which by its note alone.
unique_object: seventeen hooks, fifteen of them holding a bell

name: Brambling's Bakehouse
story: Maud bakes for the whole of Merrowby and knows what everyone eats, which is the same as knowing everything. The first loaf goes on the Toll's rim-stone every morning and is still there at noon, and she will not say why, and neither will anyone else.
who_was_here: Her husband, an unreliable huntsman, whose coat is still on the door hook.
unique_object: a coat on a hook by the door belonging to a man who has been gone nine years

name: The Bard's Room
story: One rented room over the Lip's stable. Merrick has written a verse about everyone in Merrowby except himself, and the unfinished one on the table is about the person reading it.
who_was_here: A succession of people who could not pay the Lip's rates, of whom Merrick is the current.
unique_object: an unfinished verse on the table whose subject is left blank

name: Harebell's Stillroom
story: Nell cures fevers and sells salves and refuses, absolutely, to sell anything that thins the blood, because her cousin in Foxglove Dell grows the things that do and Nell has opinions about her cousin.
who_was_here: A line of hedge-witches, none of whom wrote anything down, which Nell says is the point.
unique_object: a shelf of unlabelled jars that Nell can identify by weight in the dark

name: Osric's Forge
story: The forge has been worked by the same family for four generations, and the anvil has a dish worn into it you could set a bowl in. Osric works late because the quiet is worse than the noise.
who_was_here: His father, whose apron still hangs on the nail nobody uses.
unique_object: an anvil with a dish worn into its face and a name scratched underneath it that is not Osric's

name: Old Ashcombe's
story: Pellam kept the Wardens' Roll for forty years and still says the quiet villages' names aloud each morning, in order, because that is the job and nobody told him to stop.
who_was_here: Nobody else, ever. He has not had a guest since his wife died.
unique_object: a wall of tally sticks, four hundred of them, one per morning since he retired

name: The Eldest's Stilt-House
story: Tallissa has buried more of Isseva in the water than lives on it now, and keeps a lantern lit on the jetty rail for each one she buried herself, which is a lot of lanterns and a lot of oil.
who_was_here: Four generations of Ouls, and the water, twice, in bad years.
unique_object: a rail of forty lantern hooks facing the burial water, every one of them lit

name: The Lamp Keeper's Cottage
story: Tamsin wakes the sul-stone every dusk and turns it all night, and once, nine years ago, did not, and a fishing smack found the shingle the hard way. She says she was asleep. The gulls disagree, and so does the second logbook.
who_was_here: Six keepers before her, all of whom kept one logbook.
unique_object: two logbooks for the same nine years, kept in different handwriting by the same hand

name: The Toll's Lip
story: The inn is built into the crater rim, and its cellar is the inside of the Toll's lip: forty feet of bronze for a back wall, which keeps the ale at one temperature all year and makes every conversation down there sound like it matters.
who_was_here: Three generations of Cresswells, and everyone in Merrowby, most nights.
unique_object: a cellar wall of bronze bell, with two hundred years of names scratched into it at sitting height
